title: Console resize motion and accessibility for grid, charts, and modal overlays
creator: Maya Chen
description: Polish responsive behavior and cross-browser resilience for key console surfaces: data tables, canvas-based charts, and stacked modals. Focus areas include: smooth, interruptible resize motion; consistent overlay stacking and focus trapping; scrollbar and layout differences across Chromium/Safari/Firefox on desktop and mobile; high-DPI canvas resizing artifacts; and preserving virtualization/keyboard navigation in narrow viewports. This ticket drives a small set of prototypes and a cross-browser test plan to validate fixes, plus a lightweight spec for the engineering handoff.
goals: Ensure charts (canvas/SVG) resize without pixel artifacts or content jitter across browsers
Define interruptible, low-cost resize motion for dashboard panels and modal transitions
Standardize modal stacking rules, focus traps, and escape/focus-return behavior across routes
Ensure table virtualization + sticky headers remain accessible and usable on narrow viewports
Deliver test artifacts and engineering acceptance criteria for a single release
non_goals: Rewrite charting library — prefer pragmatic runtime fixes
Large visual redesign of dashboard panels
acceptance_criteria: Charts redraw on container size change without visible half-pixel blurs on Chrome, Firefox, and Safari on macOS and iPad Safari
When a dashboard panel is resized quickly, the resize animation is interruptible and the panel settles to final size without layout thrash
Modal overlays follow defined z-index and scroll-lock rules: only top modal traps focus, ESC closes top modal, returning focus to originating control
Tables with virtualization keep keyboard focus on the focused row when width changes and horizontal scroll appears
A cross-browser checklist (see QA notes) is complete with pass/fail for each bullet and screenshots attached
Design handoff includes a short motion spec, CSS fallback guidance, and sample JS snippets for debounce vs. throttle on resize handlers
tasks: Audit current console pages to document failing resize interactions (screenshots + repro steps)
Create two interactive prototypes in Figma: 1) panel resize with interruptible easing, 2) stacked modal behavior and focus flows
Capture minimal reproduction cases for chart redraw jitter and share with runtime/eng
Define CSS & JS guidance doc for handling resize observers, passive listeners, and transform vs width/height changes
Run cross-browser QA across desktop and iPad and collect logs/screencaptures
Handoff to ENG with acceptance criteria and link to PR template checklist
design_feedback: PM: prefer no new layout tokens — keep changes scoped to motion and stacking rules
ENG lead (R. Patel): we need repros for two worst offenders before we can estimate kernel changes
Accessibility: ensure focus return is consistent for keyboard and screenreader users; test with VoiceOver and NVDA
review_history: 2025-02-13: Initial design review with PM and ENG – agreed to prioritize chart artifacts and modal stacking
2025-02-15: Prototype walkthrough with frontend – small change: use transform-scale for preview animation, but measure repaint cost

engineering_notes_for_handoff: Do not rely solely on ResizeObserver for heavy layout work; debounce expensive redraws and keep visual placeholders during throttled updates
Prefer canvas redraw using devicePixelRatio-aware sizing to avoid half-pixel blurring (see repro-graphs)
For modals, enforce a single document-level stacking context and use inert/aria-hidden on background to simplify SR behavior
Provide sample code snippets for focus save/restore and an opt-in class for transform-based transitions
qa_notes: Test matrix: Chrome macOS (latest), Firefox macOS (latest), Safari macOS (latest), iPad Safari (latest), Windows Chrome/Edge
Checklist: redraw artifact free; keyboard focus preserved; ESC behavior; scroll lock; overlay stacking correctness; when virtualization enabled, ensure no row-offset jumps on resize
Capture 5s screencast of rapid resize on each browser and attach to ticket
Record performance metrics: FPS during resize animation and main-thread blocking for redraw
